findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, and no ACL/public access block is set, so the bucket defaults to unencrypted storage and does not explicitly restrict public access.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL or public access restriction
findings.description: The bucket has no acl attribute and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated with it, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults for public access protection.
The bucket stores ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning data is stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block despite storing model artifacts, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this appears to be a typo (likely intended as 'log-delivery-write') and its presence indicates the bucket's access control is misconfigured or non-functional, risking unintended access grants once corrected without proper review.

findings.issue_category: upload to bucket without encryption enforcement
findings.description: The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket lacking server-side encryption configuration and a bucket policy enforcing encrypted transport, so the vendor roster file is stored without guaranteed encryption at rest and could be transmitted over unencrypted channels.
